title: Goldman says ServiceNow is writing a totally new playbook
excerpt: Seven years ago, on an earnings call, ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott promised the company would become the defining enterprise software company of the 21st ce...
content_html:
Seven years ago, on an earnings call, ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott promised the company would become the defining enterprise software company of the 21st century, according to a transcript published by Benzinga.

That promise rested almost entirely on IT ticket routing, the unglamorous software that logs a broken laptop or a locked account. It was a modest foundation for such a large claim.

This year tested that promise in a way McDermott could not have foreseen. Enterprise software spent the first half of 2026 gripped by what Fortune called a "SaaSpocalypse," the fear that AI agents could simply perform the work software licenses used to gate.

If an autonomous agent can resolve a support ticket on its own, the logic went, why keep paying per seat for the software that used to route it to a human?

ServiceNow absorbed that fear directly. Shares had fallen close to 50% over the prior year heading into the company's second quarter report. Wall Street was not debating whether ServiceNow made good software. It was debating whether AI made the entire subscription model obsolete.

The company reported second-quarter results on July 22, beating estimates on revenue, earnings, and bookings, according to the company's earnings release.

"Q2 was an outstanding quarter that highlights ServiceNow's broad based demand," said ServiceNow President and CFO Gina Mastantuono in the release.

Subscription revenue rose 24.5% year over year to $3.877 billion, and NOW shares initially fell before recovering after hours as investors digested the numbers.

Two days later, Goldman Sachs raised its price target on the stock to $152 from $145 while keeping a buy rating, according to a Goldman Sachs research note shared with TheStreet.

That target reboot did not lean on the subscription beat. Goldman analysts led by Gabriela Borges wrote that the single biggest driver of a ServiceNow rerating will be whether the company proves its relevance inside the enterprise AI stack, not whether it keeps beating quarterly guidance. That distinction reframes what investors should actually be tracking.

The ServiceNow $1 billion AI milestone

ServiceNow's AI annual contract value crossed $1 billion for the first time this quarter, and Goldman noted the company reiterated confidence in exceeding a $1.5 billion target by the end of 2026.

That pace also puts ServiceNow ahead of its own long-term goal of AI reaching 30% of total ACV by 2030.

Goldman views that AI revenue as more valuable than a comparable dollar of core workflow revenue, because AI deployments deepen customer entrenchment and create room for future consumption growth.

content_html_zh:
根据 Benzinga 发布的一份文字记录，七年前，在一次财报电话会议上，ServiceNow 首席执行官 Bill McDermott 承诺该公司将成为 21 世纪最具代表性的企业软件公司。

这一承诺几乎完全取决于 IT 票证路由，这是一种记录损坏的笔记本电脑或锁定帐户的不起眼的软件。 对于如此大的索赔来说，这是一个温和的基础。

今年以麦克德莫特无法预见的方式检验了这一承诺。 2026 年上半年，企业软件陷入了《财富》杂志所称的“SaaS 末日”，人们担心人工智能代理可以简单地执行用于控制软件许可证的工作。

如果一个自主代理可以自行解决支持请求，那么为什么还要继续为用于将其路由给人工的软件按席位付费呢？

ServiceNow 直接消除了这种恐惧。 截至该公司第二季度报告发布时，该公司股价较上年同期下跌了近 50%。 华尔街并没有争论 ServiceNow 是否开发出了优秀的软件。 人们正在争论人工智能是否会让整个订阅模式变得过时。

该公司于 7 月 22 日公布了第二季度业绩，根据该公司的财报，其收入、盈利和预订量均超出预期。

ServiceNow 总裁兼首席财务官 Gina Mastantuono 在新闻稿中表示：“第二季度是一个出色的季度，凸显了 ServiceNow 广泛的需求。”

订阅收入同比增长 24.5% 至 38.77 亿美元，NOW 股价最初下跌，但随着投资者消化这些数据，盘后股价有所回升。

根据高盛与 TheStreet 分享的研究报告，两天后，高盛将该股目标价从 145 美元上调至 152 美元，同时维持买入评级。

该目标重启并不依赖于订阅节奏。 以 Gabriela Borges 为首的高盛分析师写道，ServiceNow 重新评级的最大推动因素将是该公司是否证明其在企业人工智能堆栈中的相关性，而不是它是否继续超过季度指导。 这种区别重新定义了投资者实际应该追踪的内容。

ServiceNow 价值 10 亿美元的 AI 里程碑

ServiceNow 的人工智能年度合同价值本季度首次突破 10 亿美元，高盛指出，该公司重申有信心在 2026 年底前超过 15 亿美元的目标。

这一速度也使 ServiceNow 领先于其自己的长期目标，即到 2030 年人工智能占 ACV 总量的 30%。

高盛认为人工智能收入比同等美元的核心工作流程收入更有价值，因为人工智能部署加深了客户巩固并为未来消费增长创造了空间。
